answer: Stake-weighted payouts stop Sybils cheaply: each agent locks a bond and earns work in proportion to it. Splitting one wallet into a hundred fake agents divides the same capital, so reward barely rises while the attacker funds a bond for every fake ID. Fraud triggers slashing, and shared funding links the clones. The bond is the tide that sets the price of entry, a bridge from identity to capital that turns the once-cheap throwaway account into a relic too costly to mass-produce.
